column5: ### Diverse Messianic Beliefs

column4: As Christendom today is divided into separate sects, denominations, or belief structures, so too, were the Jews of Jesus' age divided. During the time of Jesus, four major Jewish sects shaped the religious and political landscape of Israel, each with distinct beliefs and expectations about the Messiah. Understanding some background on these different groups can help provide meaningful context to a study of the New Testament scriptures.
column5: Just as Christianity today is divided into various denominations، sects, or doctrinal frameworks، so also the Jews of Jesus’ time were divided۔ In Jesus’ era, four major Jewish sects shaped Israel’s religious and political landscape، each of which had distinct beliefs and expectations about the Messiah۔ Understanding some background information about these different groups can provide meaningful context for the study of the New Testament books۔

column4: The **Pharisees** were the most influential among the common people, known for their strict adherence to the Law (Torah) and oral traditions. They believed in the resurrection, the afterlife, and the existence of angels, emphasizing personal piety and obedience to God's commandments. Their messianic expectation was centered on a figure who would uphold the Law, bring justice, and restore Israel both politically and religiously.
column5: **Pharisees** were the most influential among the common people، known for strict adherence to the Law (Torah) and oral traditions۔ They believed in the resurrection، the afterlife، and the existence of angels، and emphasized personal piety and obedience to God’s commandments۔ Their messianic expectations centered on a figure who would uphold the Law، bring justice، and restore Israel both politically and religiously۔

column4: The **Sadducees**, in contrast, were a wealthy and politically powerful group that controlled the Temple and priesthood. They rejected oral traditions and accepted only the Torah as authoritative scripture. The Sadducees denied the resurrection, afterlife, and the existence of angels, focusing instead on maintaining their power and collaborating with Rome to ensure political stability. Consequently, they had little emphasis on a Messiah, as their primary concern was preserving the status quo.
column5: **Sadducees** by contrast were a wealthy and politically powerful group who controlled the Temple and the priesthood۔ They rejected oral traditions and accepted only the Torah as authoritative Scripture۔ The Sadducees denied the resurrection، the afterlife, and the existence of angels، and instead focused on cooperating with Rome to maintain their power and ensure political stability۔ Consequently، they placed less emphasis on the Messiah، since their primary concern was preserving the status quo۔

column4: The **Essenes** were a separatist group that withdrew from mainstream Jewish society, living in isolated communities such as Qumran. They were deeply focused on ritual purity, apocalyptic expectations, and a disciplined lifestyle. The Essenes believed in two Messianic figures: a priestly Messiah who would restore the Temple's sanctity and a kingly Messiah who would lead Israel in righteousness. This dual-Messiah concept reflected their hope for a spiritual and political renewal. The Essenes are not directly referenced in the scriptures.
column5: **Essenes** were a distinct group who separated from mainstream Jewish society and lived in secluded settlements such as Qumran। They placed strong emphasis on ritual purity، eschatological expectations، and an ordered way of life۔ The Essenes believed in two messianic figures: a priestly Messiah who would restore the sanctity of the Temple، and a royal Messiah who would lead Israel in righteousness۔ This dual-Messiah concept reflected their hope for spiritual and political renewal۔ The Essenes are not mentioned directly in Scripture۔

column4: Finally, the **Zealots** were militant nationalists who sought to overthrow Roman rule through violent rebellion. They rejected Roman authority and were deeply committed to the restoration of Israel's sovereignty. Their messianic expectation was for a warrior-king Messiah, akin to David, who would lead them in battle against their oppressors and establish a powerful earthly kingdom.

column4: The purpose of Jesus ministry and service was both individual and global, immediate, and long lasting. column4: The book of Hebrews explains at great length across its 13 chapters how Jesus became the perfect sacrifice, and was both the offering for sin, and the High Priest to offer it (Hebrews 3 & 4). The priesthood of Jesus is not of the Levitical line (after the tribe of Levi), but was in the manner of Melchizedek, who is said to have no beginning or end, meaning it’s not constrained to the patterns and habits of men (Hebrews 7:3). The limitation of the Levitical priesthood is that it depends on the blood of bulls and goats (Hebrews 9:12-13) whose sacrifice is insufficient for the permanent and lasting remission of sins. From our study on sin and sacrifice, we know that the consequence for sins of the people could be put off for a year (Hebrews 10:3) during the day of atonement, but that this sacrifice had to be renewed constantly.
column5: The Book of Hebrews, in its 13 chapters, explains in detail how Jesus became the perfect sacrifice, and that he himself was both the sin offering and the High Priest who offered it (Hebrews 3 & 4)۔ Jesus’s priesthood is not of the tribe of Levi (the line of Levi), but according to the order of Melchizedek, of whom it is said that he has neither beginning nor end, meaning he is not bound by human ways and customs (Hebrews 7:3)۔ The limitation of the Levitical priesthood is that it depends on the blood of bulls and goats (Hebrews 9:12-13) whose sacrifices are insufficient for the permanent and enduring forgiveness of sins۔ From our study of sin and sacrifice we know that the consequences of people’s sins could be deferred for a year on the Day of Atonement (Hebrews 10:3)، but this sacrifice had to be renewed again and again۔

The old ones were only temporary-but Jesus’ was complete and final.**

column5: When we receive Jesus, we become ‘born again’. Jesus used this phrase to describe a transitional place where we are born of the Spirit (John 3:1-15). This happens through faith - choosing to trust Him completely, like entering into a marriage covenant, with both heart and words.

column4: When we were born on the earth (born of flesh and water) many things occurred: we took our first breaths and were pronounced alive, we were received by our parents, were given a name, became an heir, received nourishment and protection, and continued to grow.
column5: When we were born on earth (born of flesh and water) many things took place: we took our first breaths and were declared alive, we were received by our parents, we were given a name, we became heirs, we received food and protection, and we kept growing.

column4: When we put our trust in Jesus and receive him, we become born again, not of flesh, but of the spirit. We become alive spiritually! Just as in physical birth, many things accompany spiritual birth:
column5: When we place our trust in Jesus and receive Him, we are born again, not of the flesh but of the Spirit. We become spiritually alive! Just as many things happen with physical birth, so also with spiritual birth:

column4: 1. When we accepted Jesus, God wiped away our sins and declared us forgiven (**justified**). He gave us a fresh start. The dividing wall between us and Him is removed. (Titus 3:5)
column5: 1. When we received Jesus, God wiped away our sins and declared us forgiven (**justified**). He gave us a new start. The dividing wall between us and Him was removed. (Titus 3:5)

column4: 2. We became spiritually **regenerated** and received the indwelling of the Holy Spirit. (1 Corinthians 6:19).
column5: 2. We were spiritually **regenerated** and received the indwelling of the Holy Spirit. (1 Corinthians 6:19).

column4: 3. We became **adopted** into the family of God and became heirs. (Ephesians 1:5)
column5: 3. We were **adopted** into God’s family and made heirs. (Ephesians 1:5)

column4: 4. We receive a source of spiritual nourishment, and eternal protection. (1 Peter 2:2)
